daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Democratic Party chairman AHY criticized PDIP for running what he termed "grey politics." Meanwhile, the DPR deputy speaker denied accusations that the legislature merely follows the government's wishes, insisting that checks and balances remain functional. Separately, PSI expressed surprise that former President Jokowi's regional tour plans have become controversial.

  • PB PMII planned demonstrations calling for a total evaluation of President Prabowo's cabinet, with hundreds of Central Java PMII members also protesting with demands including an evaluation of the MBG program.
  • Gerindra stated that criticism of Prabowo's government is acceptable, but what becomes problematic is the intent to destroy it.
  • Ahmad Ali of PSI claimed he did not leave NasDem but was expelled, having previously spent hundreds of billions of rupiah on elections and regional elections.
  • The Temanggung DPRD will soon complete its membership through PAW processes for PPP and Golkar representatives.
  • President Prabowo is scheduled to attend the 2026 NU National Conference.
  • The location of Jokowi's political safari in Lampung has been announced.

Foreign Policy & Defence

A former Indonesian navy chief stated that the aircraft carrier grant from Italy should ideally be stationed near Natuna, though another former navy chief outlined various operational and budgetary challenges related to the carrier. Former Indonesian diplomat Hassan Wirajuda said that Iran-US tensions spur ASEAN security push, while separately an Indonesian diplomat projected US-Iran dialogue as positive despite volatility.

  • The Indonesian ambassador was invited to observe Colombia's election runoff.
  • Indonesia and Australia strengthened energy resilience cooperation amid the crisis.
  • A former general commented on plans to add territorial development battalions.
  • UNHCR appreciated Indonesia's commitment to protecting refugees.

Other

The government rolled out an economic stimulus package worth Rp 26.34 trillion, which includes eight policy measures to maintain economic growth. The stimulus includes Rp 1.54 trillion for travel ticket discounts and vocational training for 50,000 laid-off workers.

  • President Prabowo and Energy Minister Bahlil examined three PLN problems following rolling blackouts, with the PLN director reporting to Prabowo that blackouts were decreasing and a troubled power plant identified as the cause.
  • Indonesia and the UK's Imperial College London partnered to build 10 new medical campuses, while Indonesia and Japan expanded AI talent partnership through a JICA project.
  • The government maintained Minyakita HET at Rp 15,700/liter despite rising production costs.
  • President Prabowo ordered the demolition of Hotel Sultan after it was seized from Pontjo Sutowo.
  • Danantara reported to Prabowo that 258 state-owned enterprises have been consolidated.
  • Indonesia is in talks with India and Bangladesh on fertilizer exports, with Indonesia's first 47,250-tonne urea shipment having reached Australia.
